source: Written for Wayword as a learner's guide; not part of the original dataset. Examples are dataset phrases.
intro: Japanese has few sounds that English lacks, and spelling in kana is very regular. The challenges are timing and rhythm: long vowels, tiny pauses, and syllables said evenly rather than stressed.
reading: Each phrase has three lines: as written (kanji and kana), the hiragana reading, then the easy pronunciation.
No capitals here: Japanese uses pitch (a slight rise and fall), not English-style stress. Give every syllable roughly the same length and weight.
"mahs" and "des" mean the final u of ます and です is whispered or dropped, the way most people say them.
Katakana words (コーヒー, トイレ, カード) are usually borrowed from English, so they're easy wins once you can sound them out.

sounds.name: Long vowels
sounds.how: A long vowel is held for twice as long, and length changes meaning (おばさん aunt vs おばあさん grandmother). In katakana, ー marks it; in hiragana, an extra う or い after the vowel does.

sounds.name: Small tsu (a tiny pause)
sounds.how: A small っ isn't a sound: it's a one-beat pause before the next consonant, as if you were about to say it and held it. 行って is "it-te", with a catch in the middle.

sounds.symbol: ら り る れ ろ
sounds.name: The R/L sound
sounds.how: A light flick of the tongue tip just behind the top teeth: somewhere between r, l and the quick d in American "ladder". Never the curled English r.

sounds.name: Whispered vowels
sounds.how: Between voiceless consonants, or at the end after s, the vowels u and i go almost silent. です sounds like "des", 少し like "skoshi". Saying them fully isn't wrong, just a little stiff.

sounds.name: N
sounds.how: ん is a full beat on its own, and it bends toward the next sound: m before b, p or m; ng before k or g; a nasal hum at the end of a word.

sounds.name: Particles: ha → wa, wo → o
sounds.how: When は marks the topic it's said "wa", and を is said "o". That's why こんにちは ends in "wa" and コーヒーを is "koh-hee o".

sounds.name: Tsu and Fu
sounds.how: つ is "ts" as in "cats" plus a short u. ふ is a soft f made by blowing through relaxed lips, closer to an h than a hard English f.

tips_source: "How it's said" tips are written for Wayword (not part of the dataset): how a native Japanese speaker says the phrase at normal speed, next to the careful pronunciation line.

tips.good_morning: ござい runs together so it sounds like "zai" (rhymes with "eye"): oh-hah-yoh goh-zai-mahs.
tips.thank_you: とう is one long o, and ござい sounds like "zai": ah-ree-gah-toh goh-zai-mahs.
tips.excuse_me: In casual speech many people say すいません instead: swee-mah-sen. You'll hear both.
tips.how_are_you: The ん of 元気 comes before a k, so it's an ng sound: oh-geng-kee des-kah.
tips.dont_speak_well: The ん of 日本語 comes before a g, so it's an ng sound: nee-hong-goh wah ah-mah-ree hah-nah-seh-mah-sen.
tips.speak_slowly: The i of 話して is whispered (it sits between sh and t): hah-nahsh-teh moh-rah-eh-mahs-kah.
tips.learning_language: The i of して is whispered between sh and t, and ています often shrinks to てます in speech: ben-kyoh shteh-mahs.
tips.learning_by_trying: 話して has a whispered i (hah-nahsh-teh), and ています often shrinks to てます: ben-kyoh shteh-mahs.
tips.what_do_you_do: して has a whispered i, and ています often shrinks to てます: nah-nee oh shteh-mahs-kah.
tips.whats_in_this: Keep the tiny pause of the small っ in 入って: hait-teh. In speech ています often shrinks too: hait-teh-mahs-kah.
tips.dairy: Keep the tiny pause of the small っ in 入って, and ています often shrinks: nyoo-say-heen wah hait-teh-mahs-kah.
tips.live_here: でいます often shrinks to でます in speech: koh-koh nee soon-deh-mahs-kah.
tips.im_visiting: The i of 来て is whispered (between k and t): ryoh-koh deh k'teh ee-mahs, often just k'teh-mahs.
tips.nice_meeting: The i of できて is whispered (between k and t): oh-ai deh-k'teh yoh-kaht-tah des.
tips.tip_included: The u of 含まれて is whispered (between f and k): f'koo-mah-reh-teh ee-mahs-kah.
tips.very_helpful: The u of 助かります is whispered (between s and k): hon-toh nee tahs-kah-ree-mahs.
tips.recommend_food: The first す is whispered (it sits between two s sounds): ohs-soo-meh wah nan des-kah.
tips.like_talking: 話して has a whispered i: hah-nahsh-teh ee-teh tah-noh-shee des.
